comment: The case matrix of the soft-takeoff recette. runner: script = deterministic command that decides; agent = a cheap-model walkthrough that must return evidence; owner = a person (real money, real machines, a decision). status: ready | to-verify (a fact to confirm before the first run) | needs-build (something must exist first) | blocked (waits for an owner decision or a paid resource). Evidence never goes in git. light: true = part of the first, cheap wave. watch: the in-flight work whose delivery should make this case run again (cloud-budget = the session on Cloud budget and billing, slides = the session on slide creation and editing). expect: a canary, the verdict it must get. timeout: seconds, for a long case.

cases.title: Auto Routing picks from the person's list; the fallback never loops
Failures read as plain sentences, and the chat stays usable: the Kybernos model down, a bad key, out of credit
cases.brief: Two paths. (1) Kybernos model on the replica: on sandbox A send one message that works; then POST http://127.0.0.1:8822/__/engine/fail with {"match":"prov.example.test","status":503} (this fails every call to the stand-in's provider, back-up included), send again, and record the sentence. Repeat with status 429 and 401, and with {"n":1} (one failure, the next call works). Always end with {"match":""}. (2) Own key: add a custom provider with a deliberately wrong key against a real provider's address, send a message, record the sentence. For each, record the sentence, the buttons, and whether the next message (after the fix) goes through without a reload.
cases.note: Corrected 2026-11-03: scripts/fake-kybernos.mjs fakes only cloud account and invitation routes, not a model. The replica's control port 8822 is the tool: POST /__/engine/fail {match, status, n} (match is a substring of the deployment's base address; the seed's is https://prov.example.test/v1) and POST /__/engine/reply. What is NOT covered: a timeout or a 429 on an OWN key (no stand-in provider answers those; check-provider-sheet-live.mjs has a loopback fake that could grow them, README § 8 item 11). The replica keeps the failure in memory until {"match":""} or a restart.

cases.brief: On the replica, use a person who has only the welcome credit (a new account, not A: the credit is given once per mailbox). Spend it with POST http://127.0.0.1:8822/__/engine/reply {"completion": <enough tokens to pass the credit>} and one message, then send another. Record the sentence in the composer, the buttons, and where each leads (top up, upgrade). Put the stand-in back to {"completion":1}.
cases.note: To confirm before the first run: the size of welcome_credit_cents on the replica (owner setting), and that a fresh test account can be made without re-running `up` (it re-clones both sandboxes). Until then, a weaker version can play on account A by spending its 5-hour allowance (W2-02 does that).
